javax.microedition.theme
Class SkinManager

java.lang.Object
  javax.microedition.theme.SkinManager

public class SkinManager
extends java.lang.Object

Manages skins of some application in the device. Each instance of SkinManager is able to manage skins of the application it was instantiated for. An application can get an instance of SkinManager that pertains to its own skins by passing a name/version/vendor triplet related to the application. These attributes are distinct from the similarly named attributes of the skin element in the descriptor. They are dependent of the application and must be agreed between application developers and skin makers.

Using the SkinManager instance, applications can:

  • Query the skins installed for the application
  • Obtain a reference to the currently active skin, if any, of the application or any other installed skin associated with the application
  • Register to be notified about changes in the application's skins (activating another skin, updates to the customizable elements of the active skin, creations of new skins and removals of existing skins)

If no skin has been explicitly activated for the application, it is in its default skinless state, and the user interface of the application gets its appearance from the user interface toolkit that it uses. The widgets in that toolkit get their appearance from the currently active theme, which could be the system default theme or some other activated theme. It must always be possible to return the application to the default skinless state by calling the activateSkin method and passing null as the skin name.

If a skin has been activated for the application, any customizations contained in the skin for base elements or toolkit elements come into effect. The application is responsible for rendering any application-specific elements referred to from the skin.

The implementation must handle the matching of the installed skins and the application, based on the name/version/vendor triplet. If the implementation can bind the name/version/vendor triplet to a specific application instance, it should do so to prevent applications from instantiating SkinManagers that dispense other applications' skins.

In skin-related operations the name parameter must be a skin name in the form "name:version:vendor", where name, version and vendor correspond to the name, version and vendor attributes, respectively, of the skin element in the descriptor.

For example, given this skin element in the descriptor:

<skin name="foo" version="1.0" vendor="com.foobar" 
     application="MyCoolGame:3.0:com.mycoolgames">

the application would get a SkinManager instance with the method call getInstance("MyCoolGame:3.0:com.mycoolgames") and retrieve the skin using getSkin("foo:1.0:com.foobar").

Notifications about skin-related events are sent asynchronously. The method that causes the event does not have to return before the notification is sent.

Method Detail

activateSkin

public void activateSkin(java.lang.String name)
                  throws SkinException

Activates an installed skin of the application that instantiated this SkinManager. The skin that was previously active for this application, if any, is implicitly deactivated if the activation of the new skin is successful. However, if the skin being activated is the same as the currently active skin (including the default skinless state), this method does nothing.

If the activation was successful, this method must dispatch the skinActivated event to all registered listeners.

If the skin data for the named theme is invalid, or there is an implementation-specific failure, a SkinException must be thrown.

Passing null for the name parameter returns the application to itse default skinless state, and the skinActivated event is dispatched with a null value for the newSkin parameter.

Parameters:
name - the name of the skin to activate, or null to return to default skinless state
Throws:
SkinNotFoundException - if the skin to activate was not found
SkinException - if the skin cannot be activated because of invalid data or other implementation specific reason
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if name is empty, or if name is not in name:version:vendor format

addSkinListener

public void addSkinListener(SkinListener listener)

Registers a skin listener. Skin listeners need to register to get notifications of skin-related events such as the activation or deletion of a skin. This allows them to react appropriately to appearance changes, for example by repainting a custom component.

Skin listeners must implement the SkinListener interface.

If the listener has already been registered or null is passed, this method does nothing.

Parameters:
listener - the listener to register
See Also:
SkinListener

createSkin

public void createSkin(java.lang.String skinLocator,
                       java.lang.String name)
                throws SkinException,
                       ModifyNotSupportedException

Creates a skin programmatically from an appearance descriptor found using the locator passed as a parameter.

The skinLocator parameter must be a URI. The only protocol type supported is file. This allows applications to construct skins from an appearance descriptor that resides in the file system of the device, along with any media objects it refers to. If the creation of the skin is successful, the implementation must store it so that it is available for the application on its next invocation.

Because the skin creation could take considerable time, this method must not block. If the skin creation was successful, this method must dispatch the skinCreated event to registered listeners when the creation is complete. If the operation fails before skin creation can be initiated, a SkinException must be thrown.

The newly created skin is not activated by default. Applications need to use the activateSkin method to activate it.

Error conditions that must result in SkinException being thrown include:

  • No appearance descriptor found at locator
  • Descriptor not well-formed, or not valid
  • No definition for skin with given name for the application that this SkinManager was instantiated for was found in descriptor
  • Missing referred media elements
  • Skin of specified name already exists for this application
  • Insufficient resources to create skin

This method must apply the context, element and policy checks as described in the "File Format Reference" section.

Parameters:
skinLocator - the locator for the skin descriptor
name - the name of the skin to create from the descriptor
Throws:
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if skinLocator is not a valid URI, or if name does not conform to the name:version:vendor format
java.lang.NullPointerException - if skinLocator or name is null
SkinException - if there was an error creating the skin
ModifyNotSupportedException - if the implementation does not support modify operations
java.lang.SecurityException - if the application does not have the permission to manage appearances
See Also:
activateSkin(String)

getInstance

public static SkinManager getInstance(java.lang.String application)

Gets a SkinManager instance for the specified application. The application is identified using a name/version/vendor triplet of the application, corresponding excatly to the application attribute of the skin in the appearance desciptor.

If the name/version/vendor triplet can be used to positively identify an application installed in the system, it should be used to do so. Even if the application can not be identified, the appearance management subsystem must use this information to connect skins with applications.

When an instance of SkinManager has been obtained, the application can proceed to manage skins using the actual skin-related name/version/vendor triplet.

Note that it is possible to instantiate a SkinManager for a specific (name, version, vendor) triplet even if there are no skins for that combination in the repository, so that creating skins with the createSkin would be possible. Applications typically provide one or more skins in their JAR file, to be installed along with the application.

Parameters:
application - the application name/version/vendor triplet
Returns:
the manager instance
Throws:
java.lang.NullPointerException - if application is null
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if application is empty, or if application is not in name:version:vendor format

getSkin

public Skin getSkin(java.lang.String name)
             throws SkinNotFoundException

Gets the skin with the specified skin name. Applications can get a list of the skin names by calling the getSkins method and retrieving the name from each skin. The name is used as the argument for this method.

Parameters:
name - the skin name
Returns:
the skin instance
Throws:
SkinNotFoundException - if there was no skin with the specified name
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if name is empty, or if application is not in name:version:vendor format
java.lang.NullPointerException - if name is null

getSkins

public java.lang.String[] getSkins()

Returns:
an array of skin names, zero length if no skins installed

removeSkin

public void removeSkin(java.lang.String name)
                throws SkinException

Removes the specified skin from the selection of skins for the application that instantiated this SkinManager. If an attempt is made to remove the currently active skin, a SkinException must be thrown.

If the skin to remove is not found, a SkinNotFoundException must be thrown.

If the removal was successful, this method must dispatch the skinRemoved event to registered listeners.

Parameters:
name - the name of the skin to remove
Throws:
SkinNotFoundException - if the skin to remove was not found
SkinException - if the skin could not be removed, or attempted to remove the currently active skin
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if name is empty, or if name is not in name:version:vendor format
java.lang.NullPointerException - if name is null
java.lang.SecurityException - if the application does not have the permission to remove appearances

removeSkinListener

public void removeSkinListener(SkinListener listener)

Removes a skin listener. If the listener does not exist in the registry or listener is null, this method does nothing.

Parameters:
listener - the skin listener to remove
